blocks.title: gern, nicht gern, es geht so

paragraphs.text: Exercise 2a hands you ten activities and three faces — a grin, a flat mouth, a frown. The word that carries the difference is {{de:gern}}, and it covers a whole range: enjoying something, putting up with it, quietly avoiding it.
Ja, sehr gern. · Nein, nicht so gern. · Es geht so.

The question itself comes in two dressings, and choosing between them is a social decision rather than a grammatical one. Ask the wrong one and you sound either stiff or rude, so settle it before you practise the endings.
Was machen Sie gern? · Was machst du gern?

Say {{de:Sie}} to a stranger, a teacher or a new colleague; say {{de:du}} to the person sitting next to you in class. The verb endings you meet on the next page change with that choice, which is a good reason to make it early.
Three answers are worth taking as a set, because between them they cover almost anything you will be asked. A flat yes closes the conversation; an answer with a hobby in it opens one.
Ich reise gern. · Nein, nicht so gern. · Es geht so.
